AGENDA 
 
ITEM NO. 1:   
Mr. Charles Beasley, Chairman, called the meeting to order at 7:00PM. 
 
ITEM NO. 2: 
Ms. Jamie Lawson, Executive Director of Planning and Developmental Services, conducted the Roll Call and 
determined that there was a Quorum. 
 
ITEM NO. 3: 
Mr. Jonathan Sanders, Alternate Member, made a motion to approve of the minutes from the meeting held 
on August 26, 2026.  
 
Mr. Lee Roane, Member, seconded the motion. 
 
All were in favor. 
 
The minutes were approved and accepted into the record. 
 
ITEM NO. 4: Rezoning 26-007: Lisa Wittig, Applicant, to present a request to  rezone a 0.9 acre property 
located at 3383 Garden Road from the Medium Density Residential (MDR) zoning district to  the General 
Business (GB) zoning district. The property is located on the north side of Garden Road, just east of the 
intersection of Collingwood Drive and Garden Road, and consisting of Alamance County Tax Identification 
Number 112508.

2 
 
 
 
Mr. Beasley inquired if there were any conflicts of interest. There were none. 
 
Ms. Lawson gave a brief description of the item. Full packet details can be found here . Ms. Lawson stated 
that the request was for a straight Rezoning from Medium Density Residential (MDR) to General Business 
(GB). Ms. Lawson stated that the Future Land Use Designation was Suburban Residential. Ms. Lawson stated 
that the existing zoning of the property was consistent with the Future Land Use Designation, whereas the 
proposed zoning was inconsistent. Ms. Lawson stated that the subject property is surrounded by residential 
properties and that going east the area does transition to shopping areas and other businesses. Ms. Lawson 
stated that the area has a Residential Land Use pattern and that staff has concerns with the GB zoning being 
up against a MDR zoning area. Ms. Lawson stated that staff typically tries to create a transitional buffer 
zoning designation in these cases, which is not present in the subject application. Ms. Lawson stated that 
staff notified the applicants about the concerns for straight rezoning and told them that a straight rezoning 
would allow for all allowable uses under GB t o be permitted for the property, should the rezoning request 
be approved. Ms. Lawson stated that included in the Staff Report is a list of incompatible uses for the area, 
that would be included in the GB zoning.  
 
Ms. Lisa Wittig, Applicant, stated that they are wanting  to create a  R eal Estate Office on the subject 
property. Ms. Wittig stated that they chose GB due to it seeming the most consistent with other GB zoning 
designations in the area and a huge Office Institutional (OI) business in the area as well.  
 
Mr. John Hall, Owner, Stated it was going to be a Real Estate office and stated that when looking at the 
area, GB zoning is only two properties down with only one house in between. Mr. Hall stated that he has 
spoken with neighbors in the area and that none of them have any issues with their business coming there. 
Ms. Hall state d that they looked at OI but felt that GB was better suited, due to that zoning being in the 
area.  
 
Mr. Beasley inquired if the applicant was told the Staff Recommendations. Ms. Lawson stated yes.  
 
Mr. Mills inquired where the other GB zonings in the area were. A map was brought up on the screen and 
staff indicated that GB zoning was shown on the map in Red. Ms. Mills stated that the other GB zoning was 
farther away.  
 
Mr. Sartin inquired what the zoning was for the home facing the small road. Ms. Lawson stated it was zoned 
MDR.   
 
Ms. Wittig stated that the house was staying the same and no changes were being made.   
 
Mr. Beasley stated that the reasoning for the inconsistent zoning was because in five years they could sell 
the property and then that would allow the next owner to do any of the allowable uses in the GB zoning. 
Ms. Wittig stated that the Garden Market near the subject property was zoned GB and that there were 
Storage Units on the left side.   
 
Mr. Sanders inquired if they could change the rezoning to General Business - Limited Use  (GB-LU). Ms. 
Lawson stated that could be another option for the applicant and stated that the area is transitional. Ms. 
Lawson stated that the Storage Units were built in 2017  and preexisted before the current 2019 Unified 
Development Ordinance (UDO) was created. Ms. Lawson stated that if the Storage Units had come before 
the commission today, they would not have been permitted within GB.

3 
 
 
 
Mr. Beasley inquired if Neighborhood Business (NB) allowed for R eal Estate Offices. Ms. Lawson affirmed 
that they would be allowed in NB and OI. Mr. Beasley responded that would feel more transitional.  
 
Mr. Hall inquired  about Garden Market and it being GB. Mr. B easley inquired if the Garden Market was 
Conditional Business (CB). Ms. Lawson stated yes.  
 
Ms. Lawson inquired if the applicant had a Neighborhood Meeting. Ms. Wittig stated Mr . Hall had spoken 
with the neighbors, and they were fine with what they were doing.  
 
Ms. Lawson stated that through this rezoning they cannot commit to a specific use. Ms. Lawson stated that 
if the zoning were to be approved it would allow for a ny and all uses under GB to be allowed. Ms. Lawson 
stated that both Staff and the Planning and Zoning Commission has to take that into consideration.  
 
Mr. Hall stated that they chose the GB zoning because there is so much of it in the area. Ms. Wittig stated 
that OI zoning made sense for their use, but they chose GB because it existed in the area. Ms. Lawson 
requested clarification on which property they were indicating. The applicant indicated  the property they 
were referencing on the screen. Ms. Lawson stated that west beyond the Storage Units was Residentially 
zoned with one property zoned OI & GB at the corner of Saint Marks Church Rd, which is why staff states 
that the area is transitional, but in the subject direction it is Residential.  
 
Staff Recommendation: 
This parcel is zoned Medium Density Residential (MDR) and Suburban Residential Future Land Use 
designation.  The land use pattern along this stretch of Garden Road, and traveling west, is primarily 
residential in nature.  In addition to the single family d etached homes and neighborhoods, there are the 
Rivera and Preston Village Townhomes, and the Chase Apartments.  The existing development is also 
reflective of the Suburban Residential Future Land Use designation.     
 
Headed east from the subject site towards Huffman Mill Road and Interstate 40 falls, the area transitions.  
There is a portion of Office and Institutional (OI) zoned land that serves as a buffer between the Medium 
Density Residential (MDR) and General Business (GB) or Conditional Business (CB) zoning districts. The land 
uses are consistent with the Regional Commercial Future Land Use designation and include the Alamance 
Crossing shopping center, Boone Station Plaza,  various medical and business offices, the Wayfare multi-
family development, the Huffman Mill Plaza,  other retail and drive-thru restaurants.  
 
If the rezoning occurring, if the property was used as a  single family detached dwelling it would become 
non-conforming, but any of the permitted uses within the General Business (GB) zoning district could 
potentially occur. Uses such as drive -thru restaurants, gas stations, nightclubs, auto sales, service and 
towing, passenger terminals, hospitals, outpatient facilities, amongst others found in Table 4.2.C would be 
permitted although being incompatible with the adjacent residential uses and zoning districts. 
 
With the comments noted above, staff recommends denial of the request, per Option 3, as provided in the 
Consistency Statement sheet.   
 
Public Comment: 
Ms. Brianna Smith, Planning Manager, stated that staff had received calls about the item,  but no one 
submitted written comment.

4 
 
 
 
Motion: 
Mr. Roane made a motion  to recommend denial of the request to rezone a 0.9-acre property located at 
3383 Garden Road from the Medium Density Residential (MDR) zoning district to the General Business (GB) 
zoning district. The property is located on the north side of Garden Road, just east of the intersection of 
Collingwood Drive and Garden Road and consisting of Alamance County Tax Identification Number 112508. 
 
The motion is based upon the inconsistency of the proposed rezoning with the Comprehensive Plan, in that: 
• The Future Land Use Map in Section 4 “Land Use” of the Comprehensive Plan calls for this area to be  
Suburban Residential. 
• The request is incompatible with the Land Use Plan.  
• The proposed rezoning to General Business (GB) would encourage opportunities for non-residential  
development that may be non-compatible with the existing land use pattern.   
 
This action is reasonable and in the public interest, in that: 
• The request is incompatible with other residential zoning and land uses in the area. 
• The existing zoning should be retained. 
 
Mr. Mills seconded the motion.  
 
Vote (5-0): 
Denied by (Beasley, Mills, Roane, Sanders, Sartin) 
 
Mr. Roane recommended that the applicant return with the property being zoned in Office Institutional (OI), 
General Business- Limited Use (GB-LU), or Conditional Business (CB).  
 
Rezoning-26-007 received Recommended Denial. 
 
NEW BUSINESS 
There was no new business.  
 
ADJOURNMENT 
Mr. Roane made a motion to adjourn.  
 
Mr. Mills seconded the motion. 
 
All were in favor. 
 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 7:30PM.

STAFF REPORT 
Draft North Church Street Area Plan 
Planning and Zoning Commission 
October 26, 2026 
 
 
 
 
The City engaged Freese and Nichols, Inc. to develop a community driven plan for the area which extends 
along North Church Street from Vaughn Road to McKinney Street, North and South Graham Hopedale 
Road, and surrounding the areas.  The purpose of this plan is to establish a vision for redevelopment and 
reinvestment, encourage private investment while preserving the area's character, and provide 
implementation strategies to help guide future growth and revitalization.   
 
The North Church Street, Vaughn Road and Graham- Hopedale Road corridor serves  as a  major 
transportation corridor for both local and regional traffic.  It is home to a diverse mix of commercial, 
civic, institutional, recreational, and residential uses.  Despite these assets, the corridor contains several 
vacant and underutilized properties, in cluding the former Western Electric property, and has 
experienced limited reinvestment over time.  Factors contributing to this trend include inconsistent 
zoning and future land use designations, aging nonconforming uses, fragmented development patterns, 
and other barriers to redevelopment. 
 
The Plan serves as a guide for physical development and economic reinvestment along this commercial 
corridor. The planning process was guided by extensive public engagement to ensure the Plan reflects 
the community’s vision for the corridor, including two online surveys, community meetings, stakeholder 
interviews, pop-up events such as the Juneteenth Celebration, and a dedicated project website.  The 
action item provides strategies and recommendations to help implement the plan.  I 
 
A presentation by Alexis Garcia of Freese and Nichols, Inc. has been scheduled for the Planning and 
Zoning Commission meeting on October 26, 2026 at 7:00pm following a Public Open House at 6:00pm, 
at which both provide opportunities for questions and public comment.  Following the presentation to 
the Planning and Zoning Commission and their  recommendation, the Plan will be submitted to the 
Burlington City Council on November 17, 2026 as a public hearing for adoption as an amendment to the 
Burlington Comprehensive Plan.

ABOUT THE PLAN
The North Church Street Area Plan focuses on the physical development of the study area to encourage 
redevelopment and reinvestment to an important segment of a major commercial corridor and its 
surrounding development centered around North Church Street from Vaughn Road to McKinney 
Street. The Plan consists of a land use study that focuses on redevelopment and rehabilitation 
opportunities, encourages private investment in the area while maintaining the existing character, and 
sets forth a series of implementation steps that will allow the vision to be implemented.
The Plan is informed by community feedback gathered during each stage of the planning process, ensuring 
that the community’s perspectives and priorities are integrated in the Plan. The Plan is community-driven, 
inspiring shared ownership and support for its vision and goals.
Why do we need this Plan?
The City’s previously adopted Comprehensive Plan 
identifies this study area as a high-priority corridor. 
It recommends developing a corridor plan to identify 
redevelopment opportunities, guide potential public 
investments, and engage the local population in 
shaping the future of this corridor. 
How will the Plan be used?
City staff, the City Council, and the Planning and 
Zoning Commission will rely on this Plan to help 
guide decisions about development in the area. 
Additionally, City staff, and others, may use the Plan 
to pursue and support applications for grants and 
other funding opportunities, when appropriate.
What’s included in this Plan? 
This Plan analyzes existing conditions to identify the 
study area’s opportunities and constraints. Drawing 
from this analysis and community input—gathered 
through surveys, community workshops, stakeholder 
interviews, and staff feedback—a conceptual master 
plan was developed. The Plan presents design 
concepts, infill opportunities, and strategies for 
redevelopment, reinvestment, revitalization, land 
use, and property reuse. A critical component is the 
implementation section, which outlines the actions 
needed to realize the community’s vision.

Staff Report  
 
TO:  Planning and Zoning Commission 
  
FROM: Elizabeth McCarty, Assistant Planning Director 
 
SUBJECT:  Case #CZ-2025-05: Conditional Zoning Map Amendment 
Applicant: Wynnefield Forward, LLC 
 
Request to conditionally rezone four properties located at a portion of 630 Irene Avenue, a portion of 
1225 McLain Road, an Unaddressed parcel on Irene Avenue, and a portion of an Unaddressed parcel 
on Sweet Gum Street for a multifamily development. 
 
A. Actions Requested by Planning & Zoning Commission 
1. Hold Public Hearing 
2. Motion to adopt Statement of Consistency 
3. Motion to adopt Resolution to Zone  
 
B. Decision and Required Votes to Pass Requested Actions  
Section 2.3.B.(1)a of the Kannapolis Development Ordinance (KDO) allows the Planning and Zoning 
Commission to render a final decision on a rezoning request. If there is a denial, an approval by a vote 
of less than three-fourths, or an appeal of the decision, then only City Council shall have final decision-
making authority. Any final decision rendered by the Commission may be appealed within fifteen (15) 
days to City Council. 
 
C. Background & Project Overview 
The applicant, Wyn nefield Forward, LLC , is proposing to conditionally rezone  3.494 +/- combined 
acres from City of Kannapolis General Commercial (GC) and Residential 8 (R8) to Residential 18 
(R18). The rezoning request includes four parcels, with differing ownership, located at a portion of 630 
Irene Avenue, a portion of 1225 McLain Road, an Unaddressed parcel on  Irene Avenue, and a portion 
of an Unaddressed parcel on Sweet Gum Street. They are further identified as Cabarrus County Parcel 
Identification Numbers 56230575500000, 56231527510000, 56230585720000, and 56230553870000. 
 
The applicant is proposing a  multifamily development with 52 units, clubhouse, and outdoor amenities 
including a picnic shelter and playground.  Sections of the proposal  involve the redevelopment of a 
brownfields site. The site is an active eligible project through the North Carolina Brownfields Program 
administered through NCDEQ.

Planning and Zoning Commission 
 December 16, 2025 
 Case #CZ-2025-05 
 
 2 
If this rezoning request is approved, the applicant intends to subdivide the properties to align with the 
boundaries of this conditional zoning map amendment. The proposed development project has been 
approved for a wastewater allocation permit. 
 
The applicant conducted the required neighborhood meeting for a conditional rezoning on October 27, 
2025, at 6 p.m. The meeting was held at the Second Baptist Church, 807 Sweet Gum Street. A summary 
of the meeting is attached. 
 
D. Fiscal Considerations 
None 
 
E. Policy Issues  
Section 2.5.A.(2).c. of the KDO states that Amending the Zoning Map is a matter committed to 
the legislative discretion of the Planning and Zoning Commission or of the City Council, as 
authorized by this section. In determining whether to adopt or deny the proposed amendment,  
the Planning and Zoning Commission or the City Council, as applicable, may consider, and weigh 
the relevance of, whether and to what extent the proposed Zoning Map amendment: 
 
1. Is the proposed rezoning consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and other applicable 
adopted City plans?   
The subject property is within  the “Complete Neighborhood 1” and “Suburban Activity 2 ” 
Character Areas as designated in the Move Kannapolis Forward 2030 Comprehensive Plan. 
Most of the proposed development area is within the “Complete Neighborhood 1” Character 
Area which includes civic uses, single-family detached residential, and single-family attached 
residential as primary uses. Secondary uses include multifamily residential , neighborhood-
serving retail, and small format office. Desired residential density  in the “Complete 
Neighborhood 1” Character Area is 2-8 units/acre. Primary uses in the “Suburban Activity 2” 
Character Area include multifamily residential as well as retail and office. Secondary uses are 
institutional/civic, light manufacturing, and sing le-family attached residential.  The desired 
residential density in the “Suburban Activity 2” Character Area is 6- 16 units/acr e. Both 
Characters Areas support multifamily. As shown on the rezoning plan, the residential density 
of the proposed development is 14.88 units/acre. Because of the subject property’s proximity 
to S. Cannon Boul evard and its accessibility to commercial activities and public transit , the 
density of this conditional rezoning request is consistent with the goals and objectives of the 
Plan.   
 
2. Is the proposed rezoning in conflict with any provision of this Ordinance or the City Code 
of Ordinances? 
No, the proposed rezoning is not in conflict with any ordinances.  
 
3. Does the proposed rezoning correct an error in the existing zoning present at the time it 
was adopted?  
No, existing zoning is appropriate for the area. 
 
4. Does the proposed rezoning allow uses that are compatible with existing and allowed uses 
on surrounding land and with the stability and character of any adjacent residential 
neighborhoods? 
Yes, the proposed rezoning for multifamily residential is compatible with neighboring uses. 
Adjacent uses include a place of worship, single-family residential, and vacant land including 
remnants of the former Villa Mobile Home Park.

Planning and Zoning Commission 
 December 16, 2025 
 Case #CZ-2025-05 
 
 3 
 
5. Does the proposed rezoning ensure efficient development within the City, taking into 
consideration the capacity and safety of the street network, the adequacy of public 
facilities, the suitability of the land for the uses allowed under the existing zoning,  and 
other relevant considerations? 
Yes, multifamily dwellings are a suitable use allowed under the requested R18-CZ zoning. The 
street network is in place,  and wastewater allocation has been reserved for the proposed 
development. The property is in proximity to S. Cannon Boulevard and its commercial activity, 
retail, and services. The blue route of CK Rider transit runs along Cannon Boulevard. A public 
transit stop is at the intersection of S. Cannon Boulevard and Sweet Gum Street.  
 
6. Does the proposed rezoning result in a logical and orderly development pattern, taking 
into consideration the size of the subject lands and the zoning and existing and proposed 
development on surrounding lands? 
Yes, the proposed  conditional rezoning for a 52 -unit multifamily development results in a 
logical and orderly development pattern. 
 
7. Does the proposed rezoning result in significant adverse impacts on the natural 
environment, including but not limited to water, air, noise, storm water management, 
wildlife, vegetation, wetlands, and the natural functioning of the environment? 
No, there are no anticipated significant environmental impacts from rezoning this property. The 
subject properties are in the Lake Concord WS-IV Protected Area Watershed. A creek and the 
stream buffer are shown on the rezoning plan.  Additionally, wetlands are indicated on the 
rezoning plan. Sections of the site r edeveloped through the brownfields program  will be 
coordinated with NCDEQ. The proposed development will be required to conform to all 
applicable local, state, and federal environmental regulations. 
 
F. Legal Issues 
None 
 
G. Finding of Consistency with Comprehensive Plan  
Staff finds this rezoning consistent with the goals and policies of the Move Kannapolis Forward 2030 
Comprehensive Plan (“2030 Plan”) , adopted by City Council, which designates the subject property 
as located within the “Complete Neighborhood 1” and “Suburban Activity 2” Character Areas in the 
2030 Plan. Staff finds the request for rezoning compatible with the surrounding zoning and  it is not 
anticipated to have an adverse effect on the capacity or safety of the surrounding street network, nor 
anticipated to generate parking problems or any adverse impact on the environment.  
 
H. Staff Recommendation and Alternative Courses of Action 
Staff Recommendation 
The Planning and Zoning Commission may choose to approve or deny the petition as presented.  
 
Based on the request being consistent with the 2030 Plan, staff recommends approval of Zoning 
Map Amendment Case #CZ-2025-05 with the following conditions: 
1. The permitted uses allowed by this rezoning shall be limited to those uses and accessory uses 
allowed by- right in the Residential 18 (R18) zoning district. The intent of this rezoning 
submittal is to provide for a multifamily development. 
2. The number of multifamily dwelling units shall not exceed 52 as depicted on the Rezoning 
Plan. 
3. The development depicted on the Rezoning Plan is schematic in nature and is intended to show

Planning and Zoning Commission 
 December 16, 2025 
 Case #CZ-2025-05 
 
 4 
the general arrangement of such uses and improvements on the site. Accordingly, the ultimate 
layout, locations and sizes of the development and site elements depicted on the Rezoning Plan 
are graphic representations, and they may be altered or modified in accordance with the City 
of Kannapolis Development Ordinance. 
4. Perimeter buffer yards shall meet the requirements of the KDO. A Type A Buffer is required 
between the proposed multifamily dwelling use and vacant land zoned R8. A Type B Buffer is 
required adjacent to the church (civic/institutional use) and vacant land zoned General 
Commercial (GC). 
5. Road right-of-way, 30 feet from centerline, shall be dedicated along Sweet Gum Street and 
Irene Avenue. 
6. Irene Avenue shall be widened and improved according to the standards of the Land 
Development Standards Manual (LDSM) along the length of the property frontage. The full 
width of Irene Avenue shall be milled and surfaced along this same distance. 
7. Sidewalk, curb, and gutter shall be provided along the property frontage on Irene Avenue 
according to the standards of the LDSM. 
8. Sidewalk shall be installed along the frontage of S. Cannon Boulevard according to the 
standards of the LDSM. 
9. A pedestrian trail/connection shall be provided through the stream buffer from the sidewalk on 
the west side of the proposed parking lot to future sidewalk on S. Cannon Boulevard. 
10. The off-premise sign (billboard) at the intersection of S. Cannon Boulevard and Sweet Gum 
Street shall be removed. 
11. A final site plan, in compliance with the applicable Kannapolis Development Ordinance 
standards, shall be submitted to and approved by City Staff prior to issuance of a Zoning 
Clearance permit. 
 
Alternative Courses of Action 
 
Motion to Approve (2 votes) 
 
1. Should the Commission choose to approve the request for rezoning as presented in Case 
#CZ-2025-05, a motion should be made to adopt the following Statement of Consistency: 
 
Statement of Consistency: Staff finds this rezoning consistent with the goals and policies of the Move 
Kannapolis Forward 2030 Comprehensive Plan (“2030 Plan”) , adopted by City Council, which 
designates the subject propert ies as located within the “Complete Neighborhood 1” and “Suburban 
Activity 2” Character Areas in the 2030 Plan. Staff finds the request for rezoning compatible with the 
surrounding zoning and it is not anticipated to have an adverse effect on the capacity or safety of the 
surrounding street network, nor anticipated to generate parking problems or any adverse impact on the 
environment. 
 
2.  Should the Commission choose to approve Case #CZ-2025-05, a motion should be made 
to adopt the Resolution to Zone. 
 
Motion to Deny (2 votes) 
 
1. Should the Commission choose to recommend denial of Case # CZ-2025-05, a motion 
should be made to adopt the following Statement of Consistency: 
 
Statement of Consistency: The Planning and Zoning Commission finds this zoning map amendment 
as presented in Case # CZ-2025-05 to be inconsistent with the goals and policies of the Move 
Kannapolis Forward 2030 Comprehensive Plan, adopted by City Council, because (state reason(s)) 
and is unreasonable and not in the public interest because (state reason(s)).

 December 16, 2025

2. Should the Commission choose to deny Case # CZ-2025-05, a motion should be made to 
deny the Resolution to Zone. 
 
I. Attachments 
 
1. Rezoning Application  
2. Vicinity Map
